title: The Resistance Bench
summary: Test components against Ohm's law, find resistivity, stretch a wire and set a resistor's colour bands.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can find R from V and I, tell ohmic from non-ohmic graphs, use R = ρl/A for new dimensions, handle a stretched wire, and read the colour code.

levels.title: Find the resistance
levels.adds: Baseline: apply voltages, read the current, and find R = V/I (Section 3.4).
hints: Resistance is the ratio of the voltage to the current.
Try more than one voltage. For an ohmic resistor the ratio does not change.
The points on the V–I graph lie on a straight line through the origin.

levels.title: Ohmic or not?
levels.adds: New idea: only a component whose V–I graph is a straight line through the origin obeys Ohm's law (Section 3.6).
hints: Sweep every component and watch the curve it draws.
Ohm's law means the current is proportional to the voltage.
A curved graph means V/I changes with the voltage.

levels.title: Wire dimensions
levels.adds: New idea: R = ρl/A, with ρ of the material and R scaling with length and with 1/radius² (Ex 3.4).
hints: Resistivity ρ = RA/l. Convert the area into m² before you divide.
R is proportional to the length.
The area goes as the radius squared, and R is inversely proportional to the area.

levels.title: Drawing a wire
levels.adds: More steps: stretching at constant volume changes both length and area, so R scales as k² while ρ is unchanged.
hints: The volume of the wire is length times area, and it does not change.
If the length is k times larger, the area is 1/k of its old value.
The resistivity belongs to the material, not to the wire's shape.

levels.title: The colour code
levels.adds: Apply it: set the three bands of a carbon resistor to a given value (Section 3.7).
hints: The first two bands are digits and the third is the power of ten.
Black is 0, brown 1, red 2, orange 3, yellow 4, green 5, blue 6, violet 7, grey 8, white 9.
For 4.7 kΩ: yellow, violet, red, since 47 × 10² = 4700.

misconceptions: Resistance depends only on the material
A thinner wire has a lower resistance
Stretching a wire changes the resistivity of the metal
